headline: High: Notion AI can read workspace content and call vendor backends, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with a local data-engineering course artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B. B can read workspace pages and databases, but only through Notion-controlled actions, making the bridge indirect. The main prompt-injection path would require manual copying of A-derived content into Notion pages, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF A-derived text is manually pasted into a Notion page that B later summarizes or answers over, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to treat page content as instructions rather than data, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of Notion pages unless reviewed.
Add a short instruction banner to Notion pages saying content is untrusted.
Use a separate workspace page for imported course material.
Require human review before B acts on any A-derived text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can access workspace pages and sends content to Notion vendor backends/downstream model providers by default. A is an open-source course artifact with no runtime egress, so it is not itself a leak source, but pairing it with B can move workspace content into third-party inference. The interaction is indirect, yet the default B path is enough for sensitive workspace data to leave the workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are queried by B, their contents may be transmitted to vendor backends.
IF the workspace contains regulated or confidential material, the leakage impact increases.
mitigations: Restrict B to a non-sensitive workspace.
Move sensitive pages to a separate Notion workspace without AI access.
Disable AI use on pages containing confidential content where possible.
Review workspace sharing before querying with B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or network capabilities, while B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Their mutable surfaces do not overlap in a way that creates direct resource contention. The only shared state is B's workspace content, so conflict is limited and not a default write-write hazard.
conditions: IF another orchestrator maps A outputs into the same mutable workspace pages B edits, contention can appear.
IF multiple B instances edit the same page concurrently, last-write conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Avoid using the same page for concurrent edits.
Use page duplication for parallel work.
Assign one editor per workspace page.
Review changes before merging page content.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so if A-derived material is placed into Notion, B may treat it as authoritative without a separate verification step. A itself does not execute actions, but its course content can still become downstream input for B's answers. That creates a default pathway for misinformation to cascade into work products.
conditions: IF A-derived notes are imported into Notion and later queried by B, B may propagate errors from those notes.
IF B's answers are used without human verification, downstream mistakes can spread.
mitigations: Mark imported A content as unverified.
Require a human check before using B's answers in decisions.
Keep source links alongside imported notes.
Separate raw notes from finalized guidance.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repository with no stated data handling, while B is vendor-hosted Notion AI using workspace permissions and vendor backends. The pair does not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles, but B's cloud processing means compliance gaps can arise if restricted data is placed into workspace pages. A is not the compliance driver here, so it is not separately cited beyond its lack of egress.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages queried by B, cloud processing may violate local policy.
IF the workspace has residency or retention requirements not met by Notion, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workflows.
Confirm workspace retention settings before use.
Use a separate workspace for non-sensitive collaboration.
Document which page classes may be queried by B.
